utterances.text: Before I put some more questions with regard to your travel to Konjic, I would now like to ask the Trial Chamber, since the witness a year and a half ago gave the complete film, the complete tape of this interview to me, and I had given it to the Trial Chamber, I would like the Trial Chamber to allow it to have this -- to have this story shown so that we can see what exactly the interview is like. And I would like for story number 1 to be shown. The translation of the text has been given to the interpreters. Could we please see story number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is it the same film in which the witness says he has it at home did you say? The witness indicated he left his own copy at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is exactly about this uncut, unedited version of his material. He gave one version to me and I gave another copy of this material to the Prosecutor about a year and a half ago. And the witness has reconfirmed that he gave this tape to me, and I would like this -- for this tape to be shown. This is the original tape that this witness took on the premises of the barracks of Celebici. I would like the technical department to show this story. It is story number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We are here at the entrance of the makeshift health clinic in the prison in Celebici. Here you can see Serb doctors, Mr. Petko Grubac, a neuropsychiatrist, and Relja Mrkajic, an ear, nose, throat specialist. What are you doing here? Well, we happened to be in Bradina during the war activities. My colleague and I were there. He has a house there and I was in my father-in-law's weekend cottage. You are here at this clinic and you treat the prisoners. What is their condition? Well, you saw their condition. Now they are in relatively good condition. We bandage them from time to time. We give them the medicine if it is necessary and that is how we take care for their health. You say you bandage them, what kind of injuries do they have? That is to say, when were those injuries sustained? Well, their injuries were sustained as a consequence of those people being wounded. There are injuries sustained later, while they were in prison in Konjic, were sustained by some kind of grenades. You are here in this hospital, you work with your colleague, how do the prisoners feel now and what kind of injuries did the wounded sustain? The patients here are in a relatively good condition of health. This means that it is satisfactory. The wounded sustained their injuries in the sports hall while fighting and in the shelling of Konjic. Three of them were wounded there. One of them is fine, while the other two are relatively fine. The state of their wounds has improved a lot, compared to when they were brought to us. I think they will be fine in a week or two. You are a doctor here, how come you are a doctor here? Was that requested by the prisoners or was it your own initiative? I do not know if the prisoners requested that or not. However, since the prisoners were there, that is, wounded people and the persons brought in, I was told that it was necessary to phone the hospital where my colleague and I would work. You live here in Konjic, in Celebici, in Ostrozac? I live in Ostrozac. Everyday a car is sent for me. I perform medical check-ups of all prisoners, bandage the wounded and I go home again. How does the hospital in Konjic cooperate? We used to write and we still write daily needs. However, now we will write the needs for several days regarding the medicines and bandage materials. We receive enough bandage materials so the cooperation is very good. Thank you very much. Maybe just to say that we were also prisoners here, we were released just three weeks ago. At the beginning we were prisoners like everyone else and we worked as doctors in this clinic. We were released three weeks ago and now we come to work here as free doctors. Zarko Mrkajic from Bradina. I have a restaurant in Bradina and I am a prisoner of war here. I was arrested two days after fight in Bradina. How are you treated here? They treat us quite okay. The food is good. We have three meals a day. And there's enough food. Are you satisfied with the accommodations? The accommodations are okay. It is satisfying. I can see you have doctors here. The doctors come everyday. Every second day we receive parcels from home with food, fruit, vegetables and similar. So it is better than what the soldiers on the positions have? What do you mean? Well, you have food three times a day and you are delivered food from home? Yes. I do not know what they have there. The same as you have here. Ratko Cecez, from Donje Selo. I was born on the 26th of May in Donje Selo. I was brought here as a prisoner of war. I had been here in the camp. It is nice. As he said, we have three meals a day. I distribute the food. The food is good. There's some extra food that we give to the elderly who can eat more. There's enough bread. The superiors in charge of law and order are nice. We are happy with them. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, if that has an exhibit number, if we can get it into the record, what exhibit we just saw.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Defence Exhibit -- (Not on microphone).

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Regarding the transcript, in the LiveNote beginning on page 58, the full text was interpreted, but for some reason it was not typed into the transcript. Could we ensure that the court reporters listen to the audio version after the proceedings and include everything that was translated so that the transcript is complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is there any other questions to ask him?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Demic, is this the complete tape of your story that you shot in the barracks of Celebici? And during which your colleague, Jadranka Milosevic, led the interview and you were the camera person for these interviews. Do you recognise this as your materials?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, this is my story and my colleague was interviewing the persons and this is an uncut, unedited version. This is all the material that we had which we used to make the final story. Thank you. You saw the atmosphere in which we worked. You can see the details. The wish of the doctor to say something more because he probably felt that he -- this was important to say to the inmates and he was allowed to and the other guard didn't even ask him where he lived. We didn't even precisely know where they lived -- he said Ostrozac.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since this witness recognised this film as a film he made himself, and considering the relevancy of this film, I move to admit this exhibit as evidence for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any objection? It's an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Demic, you said, didn't you, that from Celebici you went towards Konjic? Actually, I would like to rephrase this question. During the year of 1992, you were always -- you resided in Pazaric and Tarcin?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: And Igman.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, when from the Celebici barracks you went towards Pazaric, you were supposed to pass through Konjic?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is known to you that at the very entrance of Konjic there is a family house of Mr. Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: I know this more because there was a disco there then because this was the house of Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean a disco, the night-club was there before the war. Is it true, Mr. Demic, that while you were passing by the house of Mr. Delalic, you happened to meet Mr. Delalic there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, about twenty metres before the gas station, which is on the right side, if you are going from the direction of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that at that time Mr. Delalic, except for greeting you, also gave you the sign to stop?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: (No audible answer)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true, Mr. Demic, that at that time Mr. Delalic told you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The answer has not come on the script. The answer to your last question has not gone on the script.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked the question if it was correct that at that time Mr. Delalic gave you a sign to stop, what did you respond?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: I said, yes, he did, about 20 metres before a gas station, which was on the right-hand side if you're going from the direction of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Demic, that at that time, Mr. Delalic informed you that a small celebration was just about to take place of the transfer of the flag with representatives of HOS and he also asked you to film this ceremony?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, this had to do with the fact that the HOS forces were to become an integral part of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at that time, Mr. Demic, stop and go into the yard of the house of Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Demic, in this yard of the house of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, is there a willow which is very well recognisable and it is situated right in the yard?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, it's behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before we continue I would like to ask you to wait for the interpretation of my questions so that the questions and the answers are not mixed up. For technical reasons, of course. So you said that this willow was behind the house. Did you at this time, Mr. Demic, inform or did you at this time, Mr. Demic, tell Mr. Delalic that you had just visited the prison in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, immediately after I greeted him and we exchanged some words, I told him that I have another story for today about the visit to the Celebici or the barracks, Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, did you personally come up with the idea to ask Mr. Delalic to say a few words about the first story that you had just finished?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: I explained to him what this was about. And I asked him to do that, but he refused to do so. And he considered that it was more important for him to do what he had suggested to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Demic, please, is it true that at that time, Mr. Zejnil Delalic told you, what does that have to do with me? Why are you asking me about these things? Were those the words of Mr. Delalic in the moment when you suggested to Mr. Delalic to make a statement?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, he said something to that effect. And, later, I think we did not give up and I think we found a compromise. We will do what is important for you, but we also need a segment of a statement to finish the story from Celebici. Because before that we passed by the house of Zvonko Zovko and we would advise anybody if they found them, anybody from the more influential people in Konjic, but we couldn't find his jeep, which was normally parked in front of the house. And this house was just four or five kilometres away from the family house of Mr. Delalic. We saw that there was no jeep, and, therefore, we went on to find somebody else whose statements we could take.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, Mr. Demic, the fact that you asked Mr. Zejnil Delalic for a statement was simply because you just happened to meet him on your way from Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, we were also a little bit short of time because we had to submit our story from a transmitter which was on Bjelasnica, the Mount Bjelasnica. And after the travel, which took about an hour and a half by car, we had to walk for another hour and twenty minutes to submit this material in Sarajevo. And we needed a couple of routine sentences.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember, Mr. Demic, where Mr. Delalic was standing at the time when you got this statement from him with regard to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, the willow was in the background, it was neutral.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you had just visited the barracks of Celebici, is there a willow in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Well, on this model you can see that there are no willows at Celebici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There's one question I would like to ask you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: On your way back to Konjic from Celebici, you must have met a number of persons, why ask Delalic alone to make a statement?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. We were driving by car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You must have seen a number of persons on the way back?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, we were driving and we couldn't meet people who were in cars also. And if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why ask Delalic alone to make a statement?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: I came to the gate and he waved to me and this was where our first discussion took place and our intent was to maybe ask the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why ask Delalic to make a statement? Did you think that he has anything to do with Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: I knew that he had nothing to do with Celebici, but I also knew that he was -- he's a logistics person, so he might have procured food, which he probably did. And our investigation went to that effect that people were being starved there. And then we also found out from the commander, Ramic, that in the same pot, food for both the fighters, the soldiers, and the inmates was prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Delalic had nothing to do with the distribution of food?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. I think he would never do such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, just for assistance of the Court, since you know I am so familiar with the Konjic area. I thought that the Court would like to know that as you're driving from Celebici back into Konjic, the very first house you come to is the house of Zejnil Delalic on the left. So I don't know if that may assist the Court or not, but, logistically, it's the first house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what I tried to explain, but the distinguished judge didn't let me finish because the distance between Celebici and the house is not big enough, it's only a couple of kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please, could you now state clearly so that it may be entered into the transcript, is the house of Zejnil Delalic the first house that you come across when you enter the Town of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Let me just reconfirm, you'd simply by chance noticed Mr. Delalic when he was exiting his house when he waved to you and then he asked you to stop?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him and his driver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Do you know the name of his driver?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: I think his name is Irfan, I-r-f-a-n.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Demic, could you please tell me whether after this event, let's say this is the first half of August, did you, after this event, ever visit the barracks of Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: After this story, there was an oath taking, maybe four or five days in Celebici and we also went to Jablanica to get gasoline and then we found out that there was an event taking place and then we dropped by. But this event was being shot by another team. And, therefore, we just had a drink, stayed there for a short while, saw how a couple of people are dressed, the soldiers. And I think it was a very great ceremony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Demic, when you say "we," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: I am referring to myself and Jadranka Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Demic, is it true that you and the reporter, Jadranka Milosevic, in this period, worked together and made numerous stories from the war areas of Hadzici, Pazaric, Igman and Konjic as well?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, and Trnovo up until Prozor, wherever it was possible. We were very mobile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Since you attended this oath taking at the barracks of Celebici, could you please tell us whether you know if Mr. Delalic as a commander of a tactic group greeted the soldiers who were taking the oath?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: In what capacity, I am not sure, but he did address the soldiers apart from other people who were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Demic, that after that time you, in these war conditions, were meeting Mr. Delalic quite often in the area of Pazaric, Taracin, Ormanje, Igman, on the battle lines for the lifting of the blockade of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, quite often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Demic, did you film an interview with Mr. Delalic as the commander of the Tactical Group No. 1?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: I think it was in Ormanje during the preparations for battle action. And I think that in that zone there was quite a lot of activity going on in that area of Ormanje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Demic, whether the battle lines of the Tactical Group 1, commanded by Mr. Delalic, were in close proximity to the lines of HVO?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Well, this was a triangle. The Serbs were in Ostrik. That is an elevation which was previously held by HVO. I don't know what the agreement was, but I believe that the HVO ceded that hill to the Serb rebels and they set up a Defence line lower down along Lepenica. While the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina held the lines on Koscan, an elevation below Ostrozac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Demic, during the interview you have filmed with Mr. Delalic in Ormanje, did Mr. Delalic indicate certain problems which existed in connection with HVO?

utterances.speaker: Bajram Demic
utterances.text: Yes, this applied particularly to HVO in Kiseljak and Kresevo, which was a specific situation throughout the war, in fact. This was a contact line between Kobiljaca and the HVO and the rebel Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I apologise to the witness and to the trial here. Here we hear "Ostrozac", the witness spoke about Mount Ostrik, between Pasaric and Kiseljak. I am drawing your attention to that for the minutes and correction should be introduced, Ostrik. I will have other questions for the witness. I don't know whether this is the correct time, Your Honour, to raise it or shall we adjourn now? Whatever Your Honour says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Since you have quite a number of questions more, we shall adjourn until tomorrow morning at 10:00 a.m. The Trial Chamber will now rise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Before we do rise, might I indicate that I will no longer be available here tomorrow and Ms. McHenry will take over for me. I will be returning the Hague in August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: 6.00 p.m., to be reconvened on the 2nd day of July, 1998, at 10.00 a.m.
